```plato

    //==
    // # Triangle, quadrilateral, and parallelogram bodies
    //
    // Area, perimeter, bounds, centroid, containment and nearest-point bodies for the
    // types declared in `planar.types.plato`, plus the classical barycentric and
    // triangle-centre toolkit (`LIBRARIES.md` ground rules 1 and 10 sanction an inline
    // `library` block in a declaration file).
    //
    // Conventions fixed here, and stated because nothing in the tree executes these
    // bodies before they ship:
    //
    //   * PLACED, not origin-centred. Every shape carries its own Center / Origin /
    //     endpoints; no body assumes the origin.
    //   * WINDING: counter-clockwise is positive. Only Quad2D has a stored vertex order
    //     that can wind either way; its `Area` takes the ABSOLUTE value of the signed
    //     shoelace area, so a clockwise quad reports a positive area. `Area` is
    //     non-negative for EVERY type here.
    //   * SELF-INTERSECTION: `Quad2D` is documented "assumed simple". For a
    //     self-intersecting quad the shoelace value is the winding-weighted area, not
    //     the area of the covered point set, and the even-odd `Contains` reports the
    //     even-odd region. Neither is repaired here.
    //   * CONTAINMENT is boundary-INCLUSIVE wherever the test is an inequality on a
    //     distance or a coordinate. The even-odd test (Quad2D) cannot honour that: a
    //     point exactly on an edge falls whichever way the floating point comparison
    //     goes.
    //
    // Shared kernels (shoelace area, polygon centroid, even-odd containment, segment
    // projection, point-array bounds) live in `geometry.library.plato`, and the
    // local-frame helpers in `lines.library.plato`; neither is respelled here.

    //==
    // # Triangle2D

    // The three vertices in stored order.
    Points(t: Triangle2D): Array<Point2D>
        => [t.A, t.B, t.C];

    // Half the magnitude of the cross product of two edge vectors — the shoelace
    // formula for three points, made non-negative.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triangle#Using_coordinates
    Area(t: Triangle2D): Number
        => TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, t.C).Abs * 0.5;

    // The SIGNED area: positive when A, B, C wind counter-clockwise (the library's
    // convention), negative when clockwise, zero when collinear. Half the signed
    // shoelace value, and distinct from `Area`, which is its absolute value. This is
    // the scalar the barycentric ratio formulas and winding tests are stated in
    // terms of, so it is named explicitly rather than left behind `Area`.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoelace_formula
    SignedArea(t: Triangle2D): Number
        => TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, t.C) * 0.5;

    // The sum of the three side lengths.
    Perimeter(t: Triangle2D): Number
        => t.A.Between(t.B).Magnitude
        + t.B.Between(t.C).Magnitude
        + t.C.Between(t.A).Magnitude;

    // The arithmetic mean of the three vertices, which for a triangle is also its
    // area centroid. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centroid#Of_a_triangle
    Centroid(t: Triangle2D): Point2D
        => ((t.A.X + t.B.X + t.C.X) / 3.0, (t.A.Y + t.B.Y + t.C.Y) / 3.0);

    // True when `point` lies in the closed triangle: the three edge orientation
    // tests agree in sign (a zero means the point is on that edge's line, so the
    // boundary is included). Winding-agnostic — it accepts either orientation.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_in_polygon
    Contains(t: Triangle2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var ab = TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, point);
        var bc = TwiceSignedArea(t.B, t.C, point);
        var ca = TwiceSignedArea(t.C, t.A, point);
        var anyNegative = ab < 0.0 || bc < 0.0 || ca < 0.0;
        var anyPositive = ab > 0.0 || bc > 0.0 || ca > 0.0;
        return (anyNegative && anyPositive).Not;
    }

    // The query point when it is inside the triangle, otherwise the nearest point
    // of the three edges.
    ClosestPoint(t: Triangle2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => t.Contains(point) ? point : t.Points.ClosestPointOnChain(true, point);

    // The triangle with all three vertices carried through the mapping.
    Deform(t: Triangle2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): Triangle2D
        => (mapping(t.A), mapping(t.B), mapping(t.C));

    //==
    // # Triangle2D orientation, barycentrics, and centers
    //
    // The classical planar-triangle toolkit the barycentric and winding lessons
    // ask for by name. `TwiceSignedArea` (geometry.library.plato) is the shared
    // orientation kernel; the barycentric weights are ratios of these signed areas.

    // The orientation of the ordered triple (a, b, c): +1 when it turns LEFT
    // (counter-clockwise), -1 when it turns RIGHT (clockwise), 0 when the three are
    // collinear. The sign of twice the signed area -- the foundational predicate of
    // computational geometry (point-in-triangle, convex hull, segment crossing).
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curve_orientation
    Orient2D(a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Integer
        => TwiceSignedArea(a, b, c).Sign;

    // The barycentric coordinates (U, V, W) of `point` with respect to the triangle:
    // the weights on A, B, C, computed as ratios of sub-triangle signed areas. They
    // sum to 1 for any point, are all non-negative exactly inside the closed
    // triangle, and are winding-independent (the common denominator carries the
    // sign). Undefined (0/0) only for a degenerate triangle.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barycentric_coordinate_system
    Barycentric(t: Triangle2D, point: Point2D): BarycentricCoordinate
    {
        var total = TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, t.C);
        var u = TwiceSignedArea(t.B, t.C, point) / total;
        var v = TwiceSignedArea(t.C, t.A, point) / total;
        var w = TwiceSignedArea(t.A, t.B, point) / total;
        return (u, v, w);
    }

    // The point A*U + B*V + C*W: the inverse of `Barycentric`, mapping a coordinate
    // triple back to its position. The affine combination is a true point for any
    // weights that sum to 1.
    Point(t: Triangle2D, b: BarycentricCoordinate): Point2D
        => (b.U * t.A.X + b.V * t.B.X + b.W * t.C.X,
            b.U * t.A.Y + b.V * t.B.Y + b.W * t.C.Y);

    // True when `point` lies in the closed triangle, tested via its barycentric
    // coordinates: all three weights non-negative. Equivalent to `Contains` but
    // written in the barycentric vocabulary the lessons teach, which fixes the
    // membership test to the same "boundary counts as inside" (>= 0) policy.
    IsInside(t: Triangle2D, point: Point2D): Boolean
    {
        var b = t.Barycentric(point);
        return b.U >= 0.0 && b.V >= 0.0 && b.W >= 0.0;
    }

    // The circumcenter: the point equidistant from all three vertices (the center
    // of the circumscribed circle), the intersection of the perpendicular
    // bisectors. Undefined (0/0) for a degenerate triangle.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circumscribed_circle#Cartesian_coordinates
    Circumcenter(t: Triangle2D): Point2D
    {
        var a2 = t.A.X.Square + t.A.Y.Square;
        var b2 = t.B.X.Square + t.B.Y.Square;
        var c2 = t.C.X.Square + t.C.Y.Square;
        var d = 2.0 * (t.A.X * (t.B.Y - t.C.Y)
            + t.B.X * (t.C.Y - t.A.Y)
            + t.C.X * (t.A.Y - t.B.Y));
        var ux = (a2 * (t.B.Y - t.C.Y) + b2 * (t.C.Y - t.A.Y) + c2 * (t.A.Y - t.B.Y)) / d;
        var uy = (a2 * (t.C.X - t.B.X) + b2 * (t.A.X - t.C.X) + c2 * (t.B.X - t.A.X)) / d;
        return (ux, uy);
    }
```
